The first release of pamble: password-encrypt a file or a whole directory into a single authenticated file, with every primitive implemented from scratch in C17.

## Install

```sh
VERSION=v1.0.0
curl -LO "https://github.com/pandalinoox/pamble/releases/download/$VERSION/pamble-$VERSION-linux-x86_64.tar.gz"
curl -LO "https://github.com/pandalinoox/pamble/releases/download/$VERSION/pamble-$VERSION-linux-x86_64.tar.gz.sha256"
sha256sum -c "pamble-$VERSION-linux-x86_64.tar.gz.sha256"
tar -xzf "pamble-$VERSION-linux-x86_64.tar.gz"
sudo install -m 755 "pamble-$VERSION-linux-x86_64/pamble" /usr/local/bin/pamble
```

The binary is statically linked and runs on any x86-64 Linux.

## Usage

```text
pamble encrypt <file-or-directory> [output-file]
pamble decrypt <encrypted-file> [output-directory]
```

`pamble encrypt photos` writes `photos.pamble`; `pamble decrypt photos.pamble` brings `photos/` back beside it. A missing output directory is created.

## What is in it

- **Archive format.** Files and directory trees in one buffer, deterministic order, permission bits kept. Extraction rejects absolute paths, `..`, and overwriting existing files.
- **SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA256,** one-shot and streaming.
- **PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256** with 600,000 iterations and a random salt per file.
- **AES-256 and AES-256-CTR,** with counter-exhaustion protection.
- **Encrypt-then-MAC pipeline.** AES-256-CTR, then HMAC-SHA256 over the header and ciphertext. The tag is checked in constant time before anything is decrypted.
- **Command-line tool.** Hidden password input (asked twice when encrypting), passwords from stdin for scripts, default output names, atomic output writes, and live progress for every stage.
- **Wiping.** Keys, intermediate state and plaintext are wiped with `explicit_bzero` on every exit path.

## Quality

- Tested against FIPS-197, NIST SP 800-38A and RFC 4231 vectors, plus tamper, truncation and path-traversal cases.
- Checked with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, clang-tidy and clang-format.
- Every module has a design document in `docs/`.

## Known limits

- Not audited. The AES S-box is a lookup table and can leak through cache timing on shared hardware.
- The whole archive is held in memory.
- Encryption runs on a single thread at about 4 MB/s; multithreaded AES-CTR and faster AES rounds are next on the roadmap.
